# Stationary Generator
Stationary generators are dedicated power installations for ships, stations and outposts. Each model has its own footprint, fuel, and atmos requirements and differing hazards. The guides below cover each generator family.
# Installation
Research and print the appropriate machine board. Assemble the machine through a frame or the Flatpacker. The Flatpacker includes standard stock parts; use an [textlink="RPED" link="MachineUpgrading"] for later upgrades.
Newly constructed machines start empty and off. Install their fuel modules or cells, add the required supplies, and start them according to the family guide.
Clear every tile the machine occupies. Rotate a flatpack before unpacking to choose its orientation. Unanchor a placed generator before rotating it. The electrical connection is at the base tile.
Connect a supported [color=yellow]MV[/color] or [color=orange]HV[/color] [textlink="power cable" link="VoltageNetworks"] and select the matching voltage.
# Inspection and Service
Examine a machine for visible condition and readable labels. Open its maintenance hatch to inspect accessible internal parts. Use an appropriate tool for measured diagnostics. Follow the generator's guide for fuel handling and servicing.
Fuel-module generators have a black solid-fuel or green liquid-fuel indicator beside the service panel. Its lamp is red when empty, amber below a quarter full, and green as fuel level rises. With no module, the indicator is a solid grey panel.
Eject removes an installed liquid tank intact only while the maintenance panel is open, stopping the machine. For a solid hopper, Eject releases whole fuel pieces and keeps the hopper installed; partial pieces remain stored. Examine the fuel gauge for the remaining quantity.
Spilled Welding Fuel, Ethanol and Plasma reagent burn when ignited in oxygen. Water and extinguisher sprays extinguish these puddle fires.
# Generator Families
[textlink="Stirling Generators" link="NFStationaryStirlingGenerators"] Generators with interchangeable solid or liquid fuel modules.
[textlink="Steam Turbines" link="NFStationarySteamGenerators"] Boilers that turn fuel heat and recirculated water into slow-ramping power.
[textlink="Combustion Engines" link="NFStationaryCombustionGenerators"] Fueled engines that use combustion.
[textlink="Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators" link="NFStationaryIsotopeGenerators"] Auxiliary generators that use finite isotope cells to generate power.
